evidence.claim: Southeast of Buffalo, the Western New York Southtowns Scenic Byway links highways through the foothills of the Allegheny Mountains.
evidence.quote: Situated southeast of metropolitan Buffalo, the Western New York Southtowns are graced with a series of highways brought together under the banner of the Western New York Southtowns Scenic Byway.

evidence.claim: US 219, NY 240 and NY 242 carry the route through those foothills.
evidence.quote: Routes US 219, NY 240, and NY 242 guide the traveler through the foothills of the Allegheny Mountains.

evidence.claim: New York State DOT describes a 108-mile scenic loop, including an alternative route, with scenic, historical, natural, cultural and recreational themes.
evidence.quote: Themes: Scenic, Historical, Natural, Cultural and Recreational Length: 108 miles (includes the important alternative route)

evidence.claim: The corridor grew when New York State legislation approved an extension through Ashford and Ellicottville to the southern Ellicottville town line.
evidence.quote: Recent New York State legislation approved its extension through Ashford and Ellicottville, terminating at the southern Ellicottville town line.

evidence.claim: That expansion put Springville and Concord in the center of the byway and brought it into Cattaraugus County.
evidence.quote: The Village of Springville and the town of Concord are in the center of the newly expanded byway.

evidence.claim: The byway organization describes its purpose as stewardship of the region’s natural, scenic, cultural, historic and recreational resources.
evidence.quote: Our Mission To promote economic development and community pride through the thoughtful stewardship of the natural, scenic, cultural, historic, and recreational resources of the byway region.

evidence.claim: brought it into Cattaraugus County
evidence.quote: The Byway’s expansion to Cattaraugus County

evidence.claim: Begin with Orchard Park and East Aurora, where the northern attractions include Orchard Park’s railroad depot and the Roycroft Campus.
evidence.quote: Historical revelations abound and a visit to Orchard Park’s Railroad Depot, the Johnson-Jolls House, and Quaker Meetinghouse are a must. The Village of East Aurora welcomes everyone to the renowned Roycroft Campus.

evidence.claim: Continue south through Colden and Concord to Springville and Scoby Dam.
evidence.quote: The Village of Springville and the town of Concord are in the center of the newly expanded byway. They beckon you to visit Scoby Dam

evidence.claim: Beyond Cattaraugus Creek, NY 240 leads through West Valley toward NY 242 and Ellicottville; US 219 forms the corridor’s western border in Cattaraugus County.
evidence.quote: Driving south on NY 240 takes you to the Hamlet of West Valley, and soon a junction with NY 242.

evidence.claim: US 219 forms the corridor’s western border in Cattaraugus County.
evidence.quote: US 219 provides western border of the Byway in Cattaraugus County.

evidence.claim: Continue south through Colden and Concord
evidence.quote: south through Boston, Colden, and Concord.

evidence.claim: toward NY 242 and Ellicottville
evidence.quote: As we continue our journey, we reach Ellicottville.

evidence.claim: A book without a publisher helped start Roycroft: Elbert Hubbard could not place Little Journeys, so he established his own private press.
evidence.quote: He was unable to find a publisher for his book Little Journeys so, inspired by Morris's Kelmscott Press, decided to set up his own private press to print the book himself, founding Roycroft Press.

evidence.claim: Influenced by William Morris, Hubbard founded the East Aurora community in 1895.
evidence.quote: Elbert Hubbard founded the community in 1895, in the village of East Aurora, New York, near Buffalo.

evidence.claim: His Arts and Crafts ideas drew printers, furniture makers, metalsmiths, leatherworkers and bookbinders into a community.
evidence.quote: His championing of the Arts and Crafts approach attracted a number of visiting craftspeople to East Aurora, and they formed a community of printers, furniture makers, metalsmiths, leathersmiths, and bookbinders.

evidence.claim: By 1910, almost 500 people had gathered there.
evidence.quote: The inspirational leadership of Hubbard attracted a group of almost 500 people by 1910

evidence.claim: Fourteen original buildings remain near South Grove and Main Street, giving the craft community a physical presence beyond its books and furniture.
evidence.quote: Fourteen original Roycroft buildings are located in the area of South Grove and Main Street in East Aurora.

evidence.claim: Influenced by William Morris
evidence.quote: Elbert Hubbard had been influenced by the ideas of William Morris on a visit to England.

evidence.claim: Springville’s former name, Fiddler’s Green, survives as the title of a mural in its post office.
evidence.quote: Springville was originally named "Fiddler's Green" before it was renamed "Springville".

evidence.claim: Victoria Hutson Huntley painted the work as part of the federal Treasury Department’s mural program.
evidence.quote: The Springville post office contains a mural, Fiddler's Green, painted in 1939 by Victoria Hutson Huntley. Federally commissioned murals were produced from 1934 to 1943 in the United States through the Section of Painting and Sculpture, later called the Section of Fine Arts, of the Treasury Department.

evidence.claim: The post office itself dates to 1936–1937: a one-story brick building in the Colonial Revival style, topped by a square cupola.
evidence.quote: It was designed and built in 1936–1937

evidence.claim: The village also turned an older building toward the arts: Springville Center for the Arts occupies the former Baptist church, built in 1869 with red brick, limestone trim and a square corner bell tower.
evidence.quote: It is housed in the historic The Baptist Church of Springville, a historic Baptist church.  It was built in 1869, and is a red brick Late Gothic Revival-style church with limestone trim.  It features a square corner bell tower.

evidence.claim: a one-story brick building in the Colonial Revival style, topped by a square cupola.
evidence.quote: The building is in the Colonial Revival style and is a one-story brick structure crowned by a square, flat-topped cupola.

evidence.claim: Cattaraugus Creek once supplied electricity here, at a hydroelectric complex built in 1925 to replace an earlier facility nearby.
evidence.quote: It is representative of a small hydroelectric generating facility of the early 20th century in Western New York.  The complex was constructed in 1925, replacing a facility near this site.

evidence.claim: The plant and dam occupy the creek’s eastern bank outside Springville, between Ashford and Concord.
evidence.quote: Scoby Power Plant and Dam is a historic dam and now defunct power plant located between the towns of Ashford and Concord, near Springville, New York.  The complex is located on the eastern bank of Cattaraugus Creek outside Springville.

evidence.claim: Springville stopped generating power at the dam in 1998.
evidence.quote: the Village of Springville ceased using the dam for power generation in 1998.

evidence.claim: Erie County then acquired the dam and surrounding land, managing it as a conservation park with few improvements or facilities.
evidence.quote: The Erie County Department of Parks, Recreation and Forestry acquired the dam and surrounding property shortly after

evidence.claim: The byway organization identifies Scoby Dam as a trout-fishing stop.
evidence.quote: They beckon you to visit Scoby Dam which boasts superb trout fishing

evidence.claim: managing it as a conservation park with few improvements or facilities.
evidence.quote: The park is managed as a "conservation park" with minimal improvements and facilities.

evidence.claim: In the northern section, the state DOT identifies Chestnut Ridge, Sprague Brook and Knox Farm parks among the scenic attractions.
evidence.quote: A drive in the Northern section of the byway reveals scenic attractions that include: the Sinking Ponds Archaeological site, Chestnut Ridge Park, Sprague Brook Park, and Knox Farm State Park.

evidence.claim: The southern extension also includes Griffis Sculpture Park, where steel sculptures have been installed on 450 acres since the early 1960s.
evidence.quote: One of the main attractions is the Griffis Sculpture Park, where steel sculptures have been continuously installed on a 450-acre park since the early 1960’s.

evidence.claim: The campus received National Historic Landmark status in 1986, recognizing this surviving art colony.
evidence.quote: Known as the "Roycroft Campus", this rare survival of an art colony was awarded National Historic Landmark status in 1986.

evidence.claim: The arts organization purchased the church in June 2007.
evidence.quote: In June 2007, the organization purchased a Baptist church dating to the 1860s.

evidence.claim: The complex entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1996, two years before Springville ended its power generation.
evidence.quote: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1996.
